newsitem.title: USA: CME January lumber down limit on weak cash.
newsitem.headline: CME January lumber down limit on weak cash.

text.p: January CME lumber futures again fell the $10.00 per thousand board foot daily limit on carryover pressure encouraged by the weak undertone to cash markets and selling linked to the break in the Dow Jones index, traders said.
At 0915 CST, January was down the limit at $389.50 per tbf with other months off $8.20 to $2.60 per tbf. March was off $8.20 at $379.00 per tbf.
The weak tone to cash lumber added to carryover pressure from Tuessday's limit loss in January to press futures. A sharp setback in the stock market early also weighed on sentiment, traders said.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce unchanged at $407 per tbf, but wholesale trade was cited in the $395 area. Demand for product waned and poor weather conditions over much of the country is slowing construction and adding to the negative ideas on cash, they added.
